title: Mentioning a history of successful loan repayment or previous profits predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention their total years of experience in their business may fund faster.
Pitches that detail specific items for purchase rather than using general categories are associated with increased funding speed for both men and women.
Female borrowers who mention expanding their business or establishing a new store may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention assets or financial history may fund slower.
Female borrowers who list a larger number of children may fund faster.
Female borrowers who emphasize their personal status in the pitch may fund faster.
Female borrowers who specify their marital status as single or widowed may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention a spouse's employment as a source of stability may fund faster.
Male borrowers who describe a specific business operational cycle may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning family responsibilities or supporting family members predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention securing the future of their family fund faster.
